title: AutoFix — AI Code Patch Generation Foundation
goal: For each confirmed finding, generate a concrete, stack-aware code patch that the developer can review and apply — moving AegisPT from remediation guidance to actionable fix delivery.
scope: Extend the finding model with an optional autofix_json field (Alembic migration). Implement an AutoFixProvider service in api/app/services/autofix.py that: (1) takes a confirmed finding with evidence refs, inventory context (detected technology, framework, language from vendor_product_fingerprints), and methodology tags; (2) calls Claude (via ChatGPT OAuth provider from backlog-56) to generate a targeted code patch — the prompt includes the specific vulnerable pattern detected in stdout_excerpt, the detected framework/language, and the fix type required by the finding class; (3) returns a structured AutoFix record containing: patch_language, patch_before (vulnerable snippet), patch_after (fixed snippet), patch_explanation, verification_command, and confidence label; (4) is disabled by default (AI_AUTOFIX_ENABLED=false); (5) fails safely — provider failure does not affect the finding. Expose autofix data through the Finding Theater API and render it in the Findings drawer as a copy-ready diff block. Add a 'Copy Fix' button that copies patch_after to clipboard. If repository integration exists (backlog-62), link to the affected file.
generation_reason: Aikido AutoFix generates merge-ready code patches for confirmed vulnerabilities. AegisPT currently provides remediation guidance text but no executable fix. AutoFix transforms AegisPT findings from 'you have a problem' to 'here is the fix, copy it'. This is a key commercial differentiator — developers act on a code patch immediately; they read remediation guidance later (or never).

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement this task until it is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Code patch generation and display only. AutoFix never automatically applies patches to any system. Patches are advisory and operator-reviewed. No file writes, no git commits, no code execution from AutoFix output. Disabled by default.

success_criteria: autofix_json field exists on the finding model with Alembic migration.
AutoFixProvider generates a structured patch for supported finding classes.
Patch includes patch_language, patch_before, patch_after, patch_explanation, verification_command.
Finding Theater API exposes autofix data.
Findings drawer renders a diff block with syntax highlighting and a Copy button.
Provider failure does not affect the finding or existing enrichment.
AutoFix never modifies any file or executes any code.
Tests cover patch generation, sparse-evidence fallback, provider failure, and no-auto-apply enforcement.
must_not_touch: Automatic application of patches to any file or system
pack registry, validation, approval, deployment, or runtime binding flows
finding schema severity or status fields

acceptance_criteria: AutoFix patch renders in Findings drawer as diff block with Copy button.
Patch is advisory only — no automatic application.
Provider failure does not break finding display.

before_promotion: Autonomous AI agent mode (backlog-60) is completed and logged.
after_completion: Update DONE_LOG.md with AutoFix implementation, patch structure, no-auto-apply enforcement.
Update CURRENT_STATE.md with AutoFix as opt-in active capability.
Promote exactly one next approved task package into NEXT_TASK.md, or set an explicit holding state if the queue is exhausted.

out_of_scope: Git commit or PR creation (covered in backlog-62)
